text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israel: riots in Gaza Strip at Palestinian Authority initiative.
- Adjustment in water agreement with Jordan will harm supply to Bet Shean valley communities.
- Industry and Trade Minister Sharansky to boycott cabinet meeting due to 'crisis in trust' with Prime Minister Netanayhu.
- Interior ministry initiating unification of Oranit settlement with three settlements.
- Ben Gurion University: Nuclear engineering department doesn't use U.S. computer.
JERUSALEM POST
- Sharansky, peeved, to boycott today's cabinet meeting.
- Egyptian envoy El Baz fails in talks.
- Price controls lifted on dairy staples.
- Bank of Israel to propose basic central bank law.
MAARIV
- Israel: Palestinian police organised riots in Gush Katif.
- Palestinian Council Speaker Abu Ala: there will be an explosion and not just in Gaza.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu and U.S. President Clinton to apparently meet in New York in ten days.
GLOBES
- Sharp drop of 25.3 percent in January-May trade deficit.
- Rise in withdrawals from savings plans, drop in withdrawals from pensions.
- Talks on 1997 budget cuts renew. Netanyahu: I'll work to increase the budget in 1998.
